questions.question: When backing a vehicle with a helper, where should the helper stand?

options.text: In front of the passenger's side.
In front of the driver's side.
Near the back of the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Near the back of the vehicle.
questions.explanation: When backing up, use a helper to watch the blind spots. The helper should stand near the back of the vehicle where the driver can see them.

questions.question: What is a danger of swerving to avoid a hazard while driving a large truck?

options.text: The truck may miss the object.
The truck may stay in the same lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The truck may flip over.
questions.explanation: Large trucks and tractors with trailers can flip over when swerving. These top-heavy vehicles are at risk of rolling during sharp turns.

questions.question: Before backing into an area with overhanging objects, what should you do?

options.text: Cut wires or branches as needed.
Get out and check the area first.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get out and check the area first.
questions.explanation: Backing up is always risky because you cannot see everything behind you. Exit your vehicle and walk the path to check for hazards, especially objects overhead that mirrors cannot show.

questions.question: When driving a new vehicle, when should you learn the controls?

options.text: Only if you feel you need to.

questions.correctAnswerText: Before you start driving.
questions.explanation: Learn where all controls and features are located before you get behind the wheel of a new vehicle.

questions.question: The more alcohol in your body:

options.text: The faster your liver will break it down.
The less effect it will have.
The longer it will take to leave your body.

questions.correctAnswerText: The longer it will take to leave your body.
questions.explanation: Your body removes alcohol at a fixed rate. The more you drink, the longer alcohol stays in your system.

questions.question: Which item is not required safety equipment in commercial vehicles?
questions.correctAnswerText: An axe.
questions.explanation: Commercial vehicles must have a fire extinguisher, reflective triangles or flares, and spare fuses. An axe is not required safety equipment.

questions.question: While driving, you should pay attention to:

options.text: Only what is ahead, not the sides.
Everything happening around all sides of your vehicle.
Only what is ahead, not behind.

questions.correctAnswerText: Everything happening around all sides of your vehicle.
questions.explanation: Always be aware of what is happening on all sides of your vehicle. Check your mirrors regularly and scan the road ahead while driving.

questions.question: Traction is important for:
questions.correctAnswerText: Safe braking.
questions.explanation: Without good traction, you cannot brake or steer safely. Keep your tires in good condition before driving.

questions.question: If you do not know how to put out a vehicle fire, what should you do?
questions.correctAnswerText: Wait for firefighters to arrive.
questions.explanation: If you are unsure which fire extinguisher to use or if hazardous materials are involved, leave the vehicle and wait for firefighters.

questions.question: If you must drive slowly and could slow down traffic, you should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your emergency flashers.
questions.explanation: If you must drive slowly, turn on your four-way flashers to warn drivers behind you (where local laws permit).

questions.question: On a curve, the posted speed limit:

options.text: Is safe for any vehicle to drive.
Can still cause a vehicle to tip over.
Is the slowest legal speed allowed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can still cause a vehicle to tip over.
questions.explanation: The posted speed limit on a curve may be safe for cars, but can be too fast for larger vehicles like trucks. A truck driver going the posted speed on a curve could cause their truck to tip over.

questions.question: Which of the following is not required emergency equipment?
questions.correctAnswerText: A flashlight
questions.explanation: All commercial trucks must have emergency equipment. This includes three red reflective triangles, three flares or six fuses, and at least one charged fire extinguisher. A flashlight is optional equipment.

questions.question: When inspecting the fifth wheel during a pre-trip inspection, you should:

options.text: Make sure there is a gap between the kingpin and the locking jaws.
Make sure the locking jaws are fully closed around the kingpin.
Make sure the locking jaws are loose.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure the locking jaws are fully closed around the kingpin.
questions.explanation: When inspecting the tractor and trailer connection, look at the fifth wheel. The locking jaws must be fully closed around the kingpin.

questions.question: Mirrors should be:

options.text: Checked only if there is a problem.

questions.correctAnswerText: Checked often.
questions.explanation: You should check your mirrors regularly while driving. This helps you know where other traffic is and spot problems with your vehicle.

questions.question: If backing a truck:

options.text: You should rely on your mirrors to guide you.
You should walk around the area first to check for obstacles.

questions.correctAnswerText: You should walk around the area first to check for obstacles.
questions.explanation: Before backing up, walk around your vehicle to check the path and look for obstacles. Mirrors have blind spots, so do not rely only on them. Use a helper when possible.

questions.question: A truck's weight:

options.text: Usually does not affect stopping distance.
Has a major effect on stopping distance.
Is less important than the cargo type for stopping distance.

questions.correctAnswerText: Has a major effect on stopping distance.
questions.explanation: A vehicle's weight is very important for stopping distance. The heavier the vehicle, the more work the brakes must do to stop it.

questions.question: In heavy traffic, the safest driving speed is:

options.text: The same speed as surrounding traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: The same speed as surrounding traffic.
questions.explanation: In heavy traffic, drive at the same speed as other vehicles. When two vehicles travel in the same direction at the same speed, they cannot hit each other.

questions.question: If you are not sure your vehicle will fit under a bridge or sign, you should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Drive slower.
questions.explanation: If you are not sure your vehicle will fit under overhead objects, slow down and take a different route if possible.

questions.question: During the vehicle inspection test, you will be asked to:

options.text: Explain why you are checking each item.

questions.correctAnswerText: Explain why you are checking each item.
questions.explanation: During the vehicle inspection test, you must inspect your vehicle completely. You must explain what you are checking and why.

questions.question: When checking power steering hoses during a pre-trip inspection, you should look for:
questions.correctAnswerText: Leaks.
questions.explanation: When inspecting power steering on a vehicle, check the hoses, pumps, and fluid level. Pay special attention to the hoses for leaks.
